  Regular Meeting Minutes
  July 11, 2024

CALL TO ORDER Vice Chair Ruiz called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Secretary Pelayo

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Sr. Secretary
Present: Vice Chair Lizette Ruiz, Secretary Edgar Pelayo and Commissioners Cyntia Esquivel and Alejanda
Flores. Chair Flores had an excused absence.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and Recreation Supervisor Donna (Nicki)
Salazar.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES FOR May 9, 2024
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz to approve the minutes as presented.
AT THIS TIME DIRECTOR COSTLEY INTRODUCED THE TWO NEW COMMISSIONERS, CYNTHIA ESQUIVEL AND ALEJANDA FLORES

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, stated that he is upset about the Parks Master Plan not
moving quicker and the delays with the Urban Orchard.

PRESENTATION
ORAL PRESENTATION OF HUMAN SERVICES ASSOCIATION ANNUAL REPORT
Catherine Villanueva, Ed.D., Director, Early Childhood Education Programs reviewed this report

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. HSA ANNUAL REPORT FOR 2023
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Commissioner Esquivel
Commissioner Flores asked what happens with children on a waiting list; there are other services available,
and they are placed in them. Secretary Pelayo asked if they offer new services; HSA has hired several social
services workers, and extended hours. She was asked to explain the Abriendo Puertas program; it is a 10-
week parent training, different topics are discussed each week. The community is asked for feedback and
what they would like offered. Vice Chair Ruiz wondered if they have workforce shortages; they have
contracted out to have the correct ratio of children to teachers.

2. SOCIAL & CULTURAL DIVISIONS REPORT FOR FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Flores
Recreation Mgr. Markel reviewed this item, a discussion ensued.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, stated that because of the street work that will be done on
Tweedy Blvd. the Christmas parade can be held on Garfield Avenue; and asked why there aren't activities

offered at Hollydale Regional Park. Director Costley explained that there aren't any buildings in which to
hold classes, but soccer and dog obedience is offered.
  Page 1 of 3
  4
 Secretary Pelayo asked about outreach and if staff can work with HSA to teach seniors about technology;
Recreation Mgr. Markel responded the department is using more social media and with the new Marketing
Coordinator and the registration software email blasts are being used. Staff is working on new classes and
activities for seniors. Commissioner Esquivel thanked Mr. Markel for his report. Vice Chair Ruiz asked if
the trip to Knott's Scary Farm was free and if use of the Golf Course has increased; no, teen participation in
their activities is low. Director Costley replied that while usage at the Golf Course has increased it will not
cover costs to offer activities even for a few people. Vice Chair Ruiz asked since the SELA Center is County
based will they collaborate with the City.

3. ANNUAL REPORT ON IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PARKS & RECREATION MASTER PLAN
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve and report to City Council.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/ Vice Chair Ruiz to approve the implementation of the Parks & Rec Master Plan
and report to City Council
Director Costley explained this item; a discussion ensued.

Recognized: Mario Dominguez, SG resident, is angry about the new Parks Master Plan; wants to know
when it will start.

Director Costley is waiting for Deputy Dir. Fierro to return so she can begin the process; maybe by the
November meeting there will be more information. Secretary Pelayo asked if the Commission could help;
no because we need to request bids and there are variables with that process, the entire process can take
up to one year.

COMMISSIONER ESQUIVEL EXCUSED HERSELF AT THIS TIME

Vice Chair Ruiz if we can get metrics, will there be comparisons with what was done and what was left to
be accomplished? Director Costley stated that yes, that is part of the Plan.

COMMISSIONER ESQUIVEL RETURNED AT THIS TIME

Commissioner Esquivel asked if the shade for the small quad be included in the Master Plan? Director
Costley explained that the Master Plan is a general idea of what the community would like, it doesn't
usually include specifics, but if improvements to the ball diamonds is requested then that could be
included; but the shades don't need to wait for the Master Plan, that can be brought back if the
Commission requests. Secretary Pelayo asked if the overhang on Diamond 1 that was removed be put back
in. Director Costley explained that it was installed originally to protect parked cars but because the way
home plate was place it didn't work, now the new fence is higher.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Explained this portion of the agenda to the new commissioners. The Fourth of July was
very busy, usually attendance is around 20,000 but this year it was only 14,000 but it was still a great day.
There have been changes in protocol and the Fire Marshall, due to the estimated crowd, was requiring a
medical tent, I explained that we don't have those kinds of problems. The Fire Marshall verified that for
the last two years there have not been injuries. Looking into hiring more staff as several have left, Sal
Campos, Fitness Coordinator just left to go to the City of Gardena.

Grounds Maint. Supv. Rodriguez: Is standing in for Parks Supt. Massey who has nothing to report. He
wants to inform the Commission that staff continues to address the gopher and irrigation challenges at all
City Parks; the brown spots at the City Hall lawn was due to a flow sensor shutting off because it detected a
Parks & Recreation Commission Minutes of July 11, 2024  Page 2 of 3
  5
 leak, it shuts down to prevent flooding, we are working on filling a fulltime position in the Facility
Maintenance Division.

Recreation Mgr. Markel: The first Concert in the Park event was held July 5, staff is working on making the
events bigger and better. More food trucks where booked, also Rec on the Run is a program with various
activities for kids to keep them occupied while the parents enjoy the music. The 3 rd Annual Fun Run event
will be July 20, lots of water, mud, slides, and lots of fun, 800 people have signed up. On August 3 & 4 will
be our first overnight Camp Out with many fun activities planned.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Vice Chair Ruiz: Sad she wasn't able to sign up for the Fun Run, thank you to all staff for all the events

Secretary Pelayo: Asked about a post that was installed at the Boy Scout Huts; staff is unsure and will check
on it. How did the beer garden and food trucks do at the Concert in the Parks? It went well,

Commissioner Esquivel: Is this the first time Family Camp Out is offered; yes, staff is very excited to host
this. Would this be offered more then just one weekend? We try to cater to the community, if it's possible
we could add another weekend.

Commissioner Flores: Is the Camp Out only for SG residents; no it's open to everyone.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS - Director Costley informed the Commissioners that Secretary
Pelayo's request about Park security will be addressed at the next meeting by a representative of the Police
Department.

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:19 p.m. Vice Chair Ruiz asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Flores

Respectfully submitted:

Edgar Pelayo, Secretary

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  August 8, 2024
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  July 16, 2024

Subject:  Review of Recreation Programs 4th Quarter FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Aquatics
The 4th quarter is typically the start of the busiest time of the year at the Swim Stadium,
and this year was no different. Our Learn-to-Swim program, which runs March through
November, picked up in April, May, and especially in June. We had over 2,000
participants register for our programs during this time, with approximately 1,000 signing
up for group lessons, almost 200 in private lessons, 200 in semi-private swim lessons,
and the rest in special events and programs. We saw an increase in all demographics
with 140 Parent & Child participants (ages 6mos-2yrs), 342 Tiny Tots (ages 3-5), 789
Youth (ages 6-17), and 76 Adults (ages 18+). In June, we launched special summer
programs such as Splash Swim Camp for kids, Gator Swim Academy, Junior Lifeguards
and Junior Water Polo. Additionally, we once again received the LA84 Grant ($25K) for
a summer full of free swim lessons; we have almost 400 registrants and counting!

During this time, we also held a Lifeguard Class (hired 3 graduates) and an Adult and
Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED course for 12 participants.  Our yearly Lifeguard
Recertification took place, and we were able to recertify 50 returning guards. We
hosted 4 swim meets, including the South-Central Swim League's Spring Championship
meet. Each swim meet attracts almost 400 swimmers with their families, and the
concessions serve as a fundraiser for partner organization SGAC.

In May, the Aquatics Team proudly received the “May as Water Safety Month
proclamation.” The Swim Stadium hosted special events Water Safety Bash and the
World's Largest Swimming Lesson, spreading the message that swimming lessons save
lives. Both events were sponsored by SGAC and had over 200 participants. Beginning
in June, hours expanded to include the return of Sunrise Swim (Mon-Thurs at 6am) and
Moonlight Lagoon (Mon-Thurs 9pm). We also saw an increase in our membership sign-
ups, especially the Splash Fitness membership thanks to the Aqua Fitness Expo we

  Page 1 of 5

  7
 held that allowed participants to sample the many aquatic fitness classes we offer. We
hosted the first of three free Community Swim Days in June. “Summer Kick Off” had
over 100 participants who enjoyed the lawn games, music, and free family swim
session. Lastly, our 3 swim teams continue to use our Swim Stadium as their practice
location, partner organizations are SGAC, Penguins Aquatic Club, and Lynwood
Marlins. Swim team participants total close to 300 children/teens.

Fitness:
Along with the Spring season and warmer temperatures, our 4 th quarter kept us busy
and continued to bring in more members. The Sports Center saw a ten percent
increase from previous quarter in memberships sold. Our most popular option
continues to be the Fitness Membership, which accounts for 3,321 of all memberships.
Across the board, the Sports Center currently has over 4,500 active memberships.
Overall, each membership category saw increases, and this can be attributed to more
families and friends looking to be more active as the weather gets nicer.

Our Group Exercise Classes remain popular. We continue to offer our staple classes
such as Zumba, Step Aerobics, Yoga, and Boot Camp. While our specialty group
exercise classes have gained traction and are developing their own following: Tone it
up, Muay Thai Conditioning, SeniorCise and Advanced Yoga.

Personal Training also saw an increase. The Personal Training program conducted
over 350 hours of training during the 4th quarter, which was almost 50% more than the
previous quarter. An increase is typically expected as the spring and summer seasons
are the busiest for Personal Training.

Lastly, our Spring Fit 5K returned on Saturday, May 11. Bimbo Bakeries was once
again our title sponsor and provided all the shirts for the event. The huge extravaganza
began at 6am as the DJ woke the community to the latest tunes, we had a vendors area
who were giving away countless freebies and food samples, and an incredible children’s
play area where participants received raffle tickets to win prizes. The successful event
had over 800 registrants, hundreds in the crowd, and remains one of our most popular
events in the Department.

Youth Sports:
All spring classes for youth fundamental sports were extremely popular and filled to
maximum capacity within the first few days of registration. Spring registrations are
typically popular due to warmer weather for outdoor sports classes. Attendance was
consistent throughout the session and participants received completion certificates
during the last day of classes.

Summer registration was on June 3 and filled to max capacity within hours. Summer is
our most popular session due to children and families on summer break. Summer
classes have begun and conclude on August 24. Youth Sports staff have done a
wonderful job of teaching the new skills and they continue to organize each class with
optimal player performance.

Adult Sports:
The 4th quarter began with multiple Adult Spring Softball divisions concluding their
  Page 2 of 5

  8
 seasons. Two champions were crowned, and they were awarded the newly re-
designed Championship hoodies, while 2nd place finishers received customized
insulated South Gate water bottles. Summer Softball league registration was from June
3-25. The Men’s league will have 2 divisions and our Coed league will have 3 divisions.
A total of 35 teams registered across all 5 divisions. The summer season will consist of
10 weeks and playoffs.

During summer break, open play volleyball continues to be one of the most popular
nights (Tuesday) of the week. There has been an increase in participation with new and
returning players consistently attending to play multiple pick-up games. Additionally, we
are one of the few locations in the area that offer open play volleyball. Staff are
currently recruiting for Men’s and Women’s Basketball and Volleyball leagues, with the
goal of beginning in the fall.

Partner Organizations (Sports):
SG Aztecs continued their pre-season football and cheer practices at Hollydale
Regional Park. Additionally, they once again participated in our Spring Fit 5K with an
informational/recruitment booth and were able to reach the community in a new
capacity.

SGJAA hosted their Spring Baseball/Softball Opening Day on Saturday, May 4.
Baseball tunes played over the loudspeaker, teams paraded across the field, and JAA
President Gil Hurtado informed the crowd that he will be stepping down at the end of
this season after being a member of the JAA for 30 years . Opening Day concluded
with free hot dogs, chips and drinks for all in attendance. Summer Basketball
registrations commenced with practices following shortly after.

AYSO is preparing for their upcoming season. Registration is currently available online
and has been conducted in person at the Sports Center.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 5,645. In the last quarter we had 6 posts and 146
stories. We have reached over 28,000 accounts and engaged with over 2,144. Our
new Recreation Marketing Coordinator oversees the Social Media Task Force and all
social media outlets.

Senior Center
Spring at the Senior Center was full steam ahead, filled with memorable events, excursions and
programming. Our goal is to promote community engagement and enrich the lives of our senior
residents by providing endless opportunities. In April, the Senior Center celebrated Easter with
a vibrant gathering that included treats, decorations, and social activities. Seniors enjoyed a
festive Easter party featuring: a fun-filled egg hunt that brought joy and laughter. Each attendee
received an assortment of Easter-themed treats, played interactive games and participated in
activities that fostered connection amongst the participants. May was a month dedicated to
honoring our beloved mothers. The Mothers Day celebration included a beautifully decorated
event where seniors gathered to celebrate. Each registered senior received a thoughtful gift,
ensuring every mother felt cherished. A variety of treats, along with games and activities tailored
to celebrate motherhood. June highlighted our appreciation for fathers with a dedicated
celebration with a delightful gathering. With a special performance by Mariachi Los Angeles our
seniors were able to sing, dance, and celebrate together in the festive atmosphere.
  Page 3 of 5

  9
 Spring also provided our registered seniors with a new series of exciting excursions, which
included visits to local casinos, LA County Fair, Temecula Balloon & Wine festival, Hollywood
Bowl, and Disney on Ice.

Contract/Youth Classes:
Spring contract class operations continued with our core offerings: baby boogie, baby Mexican
folk, ballet, tumbling, tap, hip hop, cheer, and creative dance. Classes worked persistently for 8
weeks to get up on stage and perform their routines at our culminating dance recitals. To
accommodate all classes and their families, we added in an additional recital and hosted three
evening recitals in total. Each night hosted 500 observers per show, you could feel the energy
from the performances.

Our Tiny Two’s and Tot Time classes were able to go on an excursion. Each class had the
opportunity to go to the LA County Fair complete with a class presentation in the garden and
farmhouse prior to entry.

Lil Chefs, our 5-week program was again at maximum capacity, with two classes being offered
on Tuesday evenings. Students learn two new recipes per week and enjoy their hard work at
the end of every class. In addition to learning and cooking the recipes, students are also taught
kitchen safety and the proper handling of appliances.

Special Events:
Spring season for Special events is light regarding actual events being produced and hosted.
Memorial Day was the only event to take place and that was held on May 25. This event would
not have been possible without the assistance of our guest speaker Petty Officer 2nd class Max
Garcia, Bishop Juan Carlos Mendez, Girl Scout Ambassador Lindsey Prieto, Officer Romero,
Detective Sanchez, and the South Gate Explorers. Attendees were welcomed with our
Memorial Day Program and light refreshments.

Although there were not many events to host during this quarter, the planning for the remainder
of the year started. Staff worked effortlessly to find new musical talent to bring to this year’s
Concerts in the Park. After searching the Concert series was finalized: Corazon de Mana, Los
Del Momento, Grupo Neblina, and Mariachi Divas were selected. Movies in the Park were also
planned, staff made their selections and narrowed the list down to 5 movies: Kung Fu Panda 4,
Haunted Mansion, Trolls, Wonka, and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

Cultural Arts:
Home Town Hero was the group art exhibit for the spring, this exhibit celebrated artist’s local
hero or hero’s. Our team was also able to display Dream: South Gate Senior High’s Art Show
which was a mixture of teens from freshman to seniors. For the opening we had artists, artisans,
vendors, and activities for everyone to enjoy. We designated a section of the museum to also
shine light on Hometown heroes throughout South Gate’s History. The exhibit was open for a
total of 9 weeks, many visitors came through the door to view and enjoy the terrific submissions
that were on display. On June 1 the team celebrated the closing of Home Town Hero and South
Gate Senior High’s Dream.

Not only is our museum team busy with internal programming, but they also have the
opportunity to collaborate with many other organizations. First, museum staff were invited to the
Legacy Complex for their annual Wellness Fair where they provided a watercolor activity to
promote self-care. Second, the team also started to gear up with social assets to highlight
LGBTQ+ identifying artists in celebration of Pride Month. We completed PRIDE MONTH:
  Page 4 of 5

  10
 LGBTQ+ Historical events & figures zine Volume 2 and will be providing copies at South East
High Schools Pride Festival. We also were able to guide the community through a watercolor
activity at Pride Fest. Lastly, our team also provided a collage button making activity to guests at
the Chicxs Rockerxs SELA Swapmeet & Greet in celebration and promotion of our new open
call Oír de Nuevo – Press Repeat. AAPI (Asian American & Pacific Islander) Heritage month
was in full celebration with a curated playlist and artists highlighted throughout the month of
May.

Oír de Nuevo/Press Repeat open call submissions closed Sunday, June 9 so the curation
began that following week. The museum team has been organizing and creating promotional
goods for Zine Fiesta 3 that we will host on Saturday, August 10 in conjunction with the opening
reception of Oír de Nuevo/Press Repeat.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  July 16, 2024

Subject:  Review of Grounds & Facility Maintenance 4th Quarter FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary:

Grounds Maintenance Activities
  • The Golf Course driving range net was replaced
  • Two ball washing stations were repaired.
  • Park staff extended the concrete slab on Tee #4
  • The putting greens were fertilized.
  • We repaired a three-inch water main break, and four broken lateral irrigation lines
  at Hollydale Regional Park.
  • Staff are working on raising sunken irrigation valve boxes throughout all City
  parks to prevent trip and fall hazards.
  • Public Works installed four new Park benches at the main entrance of City Hall.
  • Staff has caught over 150 Gophers throughout all City Parks this quarter.
  • We are working closely with the fence contractor at South Gate Park to avoid
  damage to the irrigation systems.
  • Renovated diamonds #1 & #4 after the fence contractor completed their work.
  • At Triangle Park we planted eight Floribunda Rose Brushes, two Crape Myrtle
  trees and added a few boulders and mulch to make it more attractive and
  welcoming to park patrons and the community.
  • Staff are coping with the recent heat waves, syringe cycling the irrigation systems
  to add additional water at all parks to ensure the turf stays green.

Park Facility Maintenance
Parks Facility Maintenance staff set up and hosted a variety of events, Memorial Day at
South Gate Park and Hollydale Regional Park, 2nd Annual Men’s Health Fair, and a Red
Cross Blood Drive just to mention a few.

  Page 1 of 2

  12
 Four new kitchen doors adjacent to the Banquet and Auditorium were installed to
replace the old and broken doors.

Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms. We use Electrostatic
Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for
indoor restroom facilities, along with a pressure washing program for the Sports Center.
We also disinfect for our set ups, events including tables, chairs, door handles, and A/V
equipment.

We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the community at two locations, one at
Circle Park and one at Hollydale Regional Park. The Community Service Worker
program is very active with many participants; assisting us in trash removal, weed
control, restroom cleaning and event setups. Parks are busy with many events,
classes, picnics, swimming, and sports activities. Outdoor pressure washing has
increased during this quarter. They are addressing high traffic areas near building
entrances, snack bar at Sports Center and the picnic areas as needed.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  July 10, 2024

Subject:  Update on Parks & Recreation Department Major Projects

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary: The Parks & Recreation Department maintains over 185 acres of
landscape and numerous community centers and support facilities throughout the City.
These parks and facilities require continual maintenance and at times major capital
improvement projects must be scheduled to keep areas safe for the public. Below is a
list of current projects slated for the Department and where they are in the process:

Auditorium Roof Project
The auditorium roof has had issues with leaking for several years and our Public Works
Department has worked diligently to provide patching. This process is no longer viable
and there is a need for a total replacement of the roof. We have secured some funding
for the project, but with costs escalating we will need additional resources. Also, if we
replace the roof, we should replace the A/C units on the roof to meet code.
Estimated cost:  $1.2 million
Current funding:  $1.2 million

Boy Scout Huts
There are eight buildings in the Boy Scout Hut area. Many have not had any
renovations since the 70’s. There are several areas of concern, the most pressing of
which is the roofs of several of the buildings. Funding was originally secured through
CDBG, but our HUD representative determined that the huts were not eligible. Designs
have been completed for the roofing at all eight buildings with an estimated cost of
$600,000+
Estimated cost:  $1,000,000 - $3,000,000
Current funding:  None at this time

South Gate Park North Playground Resurfacing
Located on the corner of Southern & Hildreth, this is the most used playground in the
City. Replacement of the rubberized surface took place earlier this year with additional
repairs to many of the pieces of equipment.
  Page 1 of 2
  14
 Circle Park
Concepts are for a total renovation of the site to include new basketball courts, a
playground, and parking. Plans have been completed and bidding has taken place. The
City is still waiting on SCE to complete their review so that we can move forward with
the project.
Estimated cost:  $7 million
Current funding:  $7 million

Hollydale Community Park
Project is currently on hold as the contractor, NRD Development, walked away from the
project at about 80% completion. The City is currently in the process of pulling the bond
for this project and getting a new contractor. The estimated time of completion is
November of this year.
Estimated cost:  $6 million
Current funding:  $6 million

South Gate Park Fence Project
This project was started in January of this year and is currently at about 70%
completion. The changes have been significant with new fencing for the Tennis Courts
(green), Swim Stadium (Blue), and baseball diamonds (silver with yellow tops). Work
still needs to be completed on diamonds #9 & #10 as well as the back of the Golf
Course and the Horseshoe Pits. Completion is estimated at the end of August.
Estimated cost:  $1,200,000
Current funding:  $1,200,000

Sports Center PA System
This project has been completed and is fully operational at the Sports Center. It is
comprised of new sound equipment throughout the facility as well as video equipment in
the exercise room and conference room.

Urban Orchard
New 7-acre park is located between the 710 freeway and the LA River. Construction is
80% complete. LA County issued a “Cease and Desist” letter shutting down
construction due to paperwork about an illegal landfill that used to be on the site in the
40’s. Testing/remediation has taken several months, but the County has now allowed
the City to move forward again with construction. This will require rebidding the project
which will take some time. The current estimate is it will be completed in spring of 2025.
Estimated cost:  $30+ million
Current funding:  $30+ million

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 4
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Nicki Salazar, Recreation Manager
Date:  July 15, 2024

Subject:  Report on Activities for Halloween

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary: This year’s Halloween Haunt will take place at South Gate Park on
Thursday, October 31, 2024, from 6 pm – 9 pm. Our Halloween Haunt event is typically
offered at Hollydale Community Park as well, but due to park renovations the space will
not be ready in time.

Staff are preparing for a complete re-vamp of this year's event. Patrons can expect a
new layout, new features and we will be using the Department’s Showmobile as the
main stage. The event will still have our annual costume contest, game booths, train
rides and DJ. The costume contest will be judged by volunteers such as our City
Council and Parks & Recreation Commissioners, who will have the tough decision to
award winners in three categories for every age group. Our game booths will line the
outfield of Diamond 3 and are sure to be an interactive challenge for all our patrons to
enjoy. Lastly, our train rides will be operating on Diamond 4 and will drive on a
continuous loop to accommodate 16-24 riders per trip. The events DJ will be playing
today’s hits mixed in with a few Halloween classics.

South Gate residents are going to enjoy the new features as patrons can expect the
return of our Haunted Maze, Halloween themed inflatables and an interactive inflatable
that will be available for all to enjoy. Inflatables will be clustered and designated per age
group to ensure all patrons have a safe experience, we will also be providing a toddler
soft play area to guarantee all ages are accommodated. Two new DIY stations will be
available for patrons: Make and take your own Halloween slime and a Halloween cookie
decorating station. Photo opportunities will be spread throughout the event with newly
designed sets and backdrops, along with an interactive photobooth that will print and
text photos. Our team has also added food truck opportunities accompanied by a
Halloween themed seating area for patrons to enjoy snacks and desserts.

Led by Recreation Coordinator Salomon Lopez, this Halloween is sure to be a scary
good time. His team has already begun preparations for the event along with designing
and finalizing all marketing materials.
